title: Encoding, Buffering and Safe Resource Management

understand.concept: Text is encoded as bytes using a charset. The same characters can produce different bytes under different encodings. Use UTF-8 explicitly, process large content incrementally and use try-with-resources.

explain.narrative:
## Encoding, Buffering and Safe Resource Management

Text is encoded as bytes using a charset. The same characters can produce different bytes under different encodings. Use UTF-8 explicitly, process large content incrementally and use try-with-resources.

Identify the input and desired result. Select the Java construct or API that supports the requirement. Keep code readable, handle documented failures and state assumptions clearly.

Compile with JDK 21, predict output before running, and test normal, boundary and invalid inputs.

examples.title: Core API
examples.code: public class Main { public static void main(String[] args) throws Exception { byte[] bytes = "café".getBytes(java.nio.charset.StandardCharsets.UTF_8); System.out.println(bytes.length); } }
examples.explanation: UTF-8 encodes the string into five bytes.

examples.title: Practical use
examples.code: public class Main { public static void main(String[] args) throws Exception { String restored = new String("Code".getBytes(java.nio.charset.StandardCharsets.UTF_8), java.nio.charset.StandardCharsets.UTF_8); System.out.println(restored); } }
examples.explanation: Decodes bytes using the same explicit charset.

examples.title: Boundary behavior
examples.code: public class Main { public static void main(String[] args) throws Exception { System.out.println("A".length() + ":" + "é".getBytes(java.nio.charset.StandardCharsets.UTF_8).length); } }
examples.explanation: Shows that a Java String length and its UTF-8 byte count are different measures.

examples.title: Alternative pattern
examples.code: public class Main { public static void main(String[] args) throws Exception { try (var writer = new java.io.StringWriter(); var buffered = new java.io.BufferedWriter(writer)) { buffered.write("safe"); buffered.flush(); System.out.println(writer); } } }

examples.title: Verify the result
examples.code: public class Main { public static void main(String[] args) throws Exception { System.out.println("Process chunks instead of loading a very large file at once"); } }
examples.expectedOutput: Process chunks instead of loading a very large file at once
examples.explanation: States the memory-safety principle for large streams.
